title: Orbital-selective band evolution and out-of-plane correlation in the FeGe-family kagome antiferromagnet ScFe$_6$Ge$_6$
authors: Jae Hyuck Lee, Ze Yan, Tongrui Li, Yichen Yang, Dirk Wulferding, Jongkeun Jung, Zhicheng Jiang, Mao Ye, Zhengtai Liu, Changyoung Kim, Soohyun Cho, Yanfeng Guo, Dawei Shen
abstract: In strongly correlated materials such as high-temperature superconductors, the relation between charge density wave (CDW) order and magnetism remains an important unresolved problem. FeGe is the first kagome metal known to exhibit CDW order deep within an antiferromagnetic state, accompanied by an unconventional evolution of lattice symmetry. To elucidate the general conditions governing such spin-correlated CDW order, we investigate ScFe$_6$Ge$_6$, which lacks CDW order and therefore exhibits reduced involvement of charge degrees of freedom while retaining other properties of FeGe. Instead of a CDW order, ScFe$_6$Ge$_6$ undergoes a magnetic transition at $T^*$ = 195 K. Across this transition, angle-resolved photoemission and Raman spectroscopy reveal orbital-selective behavior confined to a single kagome Dirac band, together with electron-phonon and magnetoelastic coupling to an out-of-plane phonon mode. These results suggest that orbital-selective physics and out-of-plane correlations play enhanced roles in realizing spin-correlated CDW order in magnetic kagome metals.
summary: This work investigates the complex interplay between magnetism, orbital physics, and lattice vibrations in kagome antiferromagnets like $	ext{ScFe}_6	ext{Ge}_6$. By comparing it to a CDW-hosting analogue ($	ext{FeGe}$), the researchers show that while charge order is absent in $	ext{ScFe}_6	ext{Ge}_6$, its magnetic transition ($T^*$) is marked by orbital-selective band shifts and magnetoelastic coupling. This highlights that out-of-plane correlations and orbital degrees of freedom are crucial drivers in these correlated materials.
main_problem: The research aims to understand the general conditions governing spin-correlated Charge Density Wave (CDW) order in kagome antiferromagnets, contrasting systems that exhibit CDW with those that do not.
main_result: In $	ext{ScFe}_6	ext{Ge}_6$, a magnetic transition at $T^*=195 	ext{ K}$ is linked to orbital-selective band shifts and magnetoelastic coupling involving out-of-plane phonon modes, suggesting orbital physics plays a key role where CDW order is absent.
method: The study combines multiple experimental techniques including Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES), Raman spectroscopy, and magnetic/resistivity measurements, supplemented by theoretical calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is the FeGe-family of kagome antiferromagnets, specifically comparing $	ext{FeGe}$ (CDW exhibiting) with $	ext{ScFe}_6	ext{Ge}_6$ (lacking CDW). The focus is on the interplay between spin, orbital, lattice, and charge degrees of freedom.
key_observables: Orbital-selective band shifts ($	ext{ARPES}$), anomalous kinks in phonon frequencies ($	ext{Raman}$), magnetic susceptibility ($\chi(T)$), and resistivity ($ho(T)$).
important_parameters: $T^* = 195 	ext{ K}$ (magnetic transition temperature); $\lambda \approx 0.3$ (electron-phonon coupling constant).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on assigning specific orbital characters ($	ext{dz}^2$) to the observed electronic bands based on polarization dependence and analogy with known materials.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate structural details, magnetic susceptibility curves, $	ext{ARPES}$ spectra showing Dirac cones and band shifts across $T^*$, and Raman spectra revealing an anomalous kink in the out-of-plane phonon mode near $T^*$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares $	ext{ScFe}_6	ext{Ge}_6$ to $	ext{FeGe}$, using structural, magnetic, electronic ($	ext{ARPES}$), and vibrational ($	ext{Raman}$) measurements to pinpoint the mechanism driving anomalies at $T^*$, ultimately arguing for the enhanced role of orbital-selective physics.
why_interesting: The detailed investigation into how subtle changes in spin order (magnetoelastic coupling) can manifest as measurable electronic band shifts or phonon anomalies provides a rich platform for studying coupled quantum orders, relevant to understanding emergent phenomena in strongly correlated systems.
